name: Lucrecia Dalt
label: RVNG Intl.
lede: A Colombian soil engineer who turned into a Berlin voice artist, and in 2022 an alien in a Spanish-language bolero record that Pitchfork ranked No. 8 of the year.

eras.title: A soil engineer with a maraca
eras.text: Born in Pereira, trained as a civil engineer, and making electronic music in Medellín on the side. Her first records came out through Colombian labels and the Series collective, under the name Lucrecia.

years.src: Chain DLK: Lucrecia Dalt · Digital in Berlin: Lucrecia Dalt · Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt
years.p: Her grandfather played drums and maracas, and her mother played her bambucos, pasillos, boleros and Spanish ballads.
years.xp:
Dalt says her grandfather taught her to play maracas when she was four, and that her mother exposed her to Colombian folk forms: bambucos, pasillos, currulaos, guabinas, boleros.

Those boleros come back two decades later as the rhythmic spine of ¡Ay!.

years.cap: Medellín, where Dalt worked as an engineer and started making music.
years.src: Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt · Chain DLK: Lucrecia Dalt · CLOT: Lucrecia Dalt, earthly encounters
years.h: A geotechnical engineer by day, electronic producer by night
years.p: Dalt studied civil engineering and worked on soil and construction problems in Medellín, and started making music around 2004.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia she spent two years at a geotechnical company in Medellín. Chain DLK puts her in Medellín for eight years before she left for Europe.

In Colombia she got involved with the electronic collective Series Media, which put out her first records.

years.p: Her first album came out on Mil Records, with a re-edit on Series the same year, under her first name only.

years.h: Like Being Home EP lands on Series
years.p: Her second release on the Colombian collective, still billed as Lucrecia, before the full name and the move to Europe.

eras.title: Found on MySpace, relocated to Europe
eras.text: A German producer heard her online, and Dalt left for Barcelona and later Berlin. A run of albums on Human Ear Music and a tour with Julia Holter follow.

years.src: Chain DLK: Lucrecia Dalt · Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt
years.p: The Berlin producer heard her online and put her on the compilation 4 Women No Cry on Monika Enterprise.
years.xp:
Chain DLK reports that Dalt was discovered through MySpace by Gut, which led to the 4 Women No Cry compilation in 2008. The same compilation is where she met [[Julia Holter|45610c1f-41a4-44f1-9da6-227510073ffc]].

She lived in Barcelona before settling in Berlin.

years.p: Released on Pruna Recordings, after the 4 Women No Cry appearance.

years.h: Commotus opens the Human Ear Music run
years.p: Her first album on Human Ear Music, followed by Syzygy in 2013.
Released in 2013 on Human Ear Music, a year after Commotus.
The two had met through the 4 Women No Cry compilation, and Holter took her on the road in Europe from October 24.

years.src: CLOT: Lucrecia Dalt, earthly encounters · Crack Magazine: The phantasmagoric poetics of Lucrecia Dalt · Wikipedia: Lucrecia Dalt
years.p: The pair have worked together since 2014 on the politics of listening, including the audiovisual mystic opera V.I.T.R.I.O.L.. The same year she put out a self-titled EP on [[Nicolás Jaar|06e99a1b-4020-4380-ab27-1a3e0c5e557c]]'s Other People.
Released on Care Of Editions, the imprint that also put out her 12-inch around this time.

eras.title: The voice takes over
eras.text: On RVNG Intl. she strips her sound down to synths and her own processed voice. Two albums in two years, then a run of noise collaborations on the side.

years.src: Wikipedia: Anticlines (album) · CLOT: Lucrecia Dalt, earthly encounters
years.p: Dalt says every sound on the record is either her voice or a synth run through processing. Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
She built it mainly on a Nord Modular and a Moogerfooger MuRF, with lyrics co-written with Henry Anderson. Pitchfork's Philip Sherburne singled out its vocal dimension, including spoken-word passages with subtle processing.

Videos followed for "Edge" and "Tar".

years.src: Wikipedia: No Era Sólida · Crack Magazine: The phantasmagoric poetics of Lucrecia Dalt · Subbacultcha: An Interview with Lucrecia Dalt
years.h: No Era Sólida: an album that dissolves on purpose
years.p: Recorded and mixed by Dalt herself in Berlin, at INA GRM in Paris and at Pioneer Works in Brooklyn. Pitchfork gave it 7.9.
years.xp:
The album follows a fictional character, Lia, drawn from a J.G. Ballard short story and Clarice Lispector's novel A Breath of Life. Part of the sales went to Tierra Digna, which supports Colombian communities.

She has said the first song was a complete improvisation, after hours of listening to singers in languages she doesn't know.

years.p: The Hanson release, plus two EPs, Demands of Ordinary Devotion and The Blob, teamed her with the former [[Wolf Eyes|51ff6576-95ff-4e02-a0cf-fad3b39c0b8d]] member on his label.

eras.title: Preta lands
eras.text: An alien in a bought human body, a Spanish-language bolero record, and the year Dalt went from quiet favorite to critics' favorite. She also scored a horror film and an HBO series.

years.src: Spitfire Audio: Lucrecia Dalt talks loud scores
years.h: Two scores: The Seed and HBO's The Baby
years.p: Her first film score was for Sam Walker's horror film The Seed; the The Baby score followed. Both were released on Invada.
years.xp:
For The Baby she recorded herself, her partner and drummer Alex Lázaro, vocalist Audrey Chen and Canadian throat singer Cynthia Pitsiulak on ribbon microphones.

She has said she likes working with directors who want the score "present and loud".

years.h: "No Tiempo" shows up with a short film
years.p: The lead single opens with a sustained organ chord; the film was directed by Aina Climent.
years.xp: The FADER made it a Song You Need on July 19, calling out the organ chord that unwinds into an orchestral arrangement.

q: She is really worried about humanity's obsession with time.
years.src: Subbacultcha: An Interview with Lucrecia Dalt · The FADER: Song You Need · Wikipedia: ¡Ay!
years.h: Preta buys a body in a hydrosphere market
years.p: Dalt and philosopher Miguel Prado wrote the script for ¡Ay!, about an alien who purchases a human body and worries about humans' obsession with time.
years.xp:
The album is sung entirely in Spanish and leans on bolero-shaped rhythms, played on acoustic instruments. Dalt describes "Atemporal" as a collection of Dalts from different eras, with vocoders, synths and processed drums.

Videos also went out for "Dicen" and "Enviada".

years.h: ¡Ay! on RVNG Intl.: Pitchfork 8.6, No. 8 of 2022
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.6 and ranked it No. 8 of 2022; Metacritic lists it at 83. The Wire made it record of the year.
years.xp:
Trumpeter Lina Allemano and percussionist Alex Lázaro play on it, and Marta Salogni mixed it. The 34-minute album is her first solo release since No Era Sólida.

Scores cited from Wikipedia's reception box (Pitchfork 8.6, Metacritic 83).

years.h: The Wire's record of the year
years.p: The magazine named ¡Ay! its No. 1 of 2022.

eras.title: A Danger to Ourselves
eras.text: With David Sylvian co-producing and another soundtrack out, Dalt follows the Preta record with a pop-adjacent, stranger one.

years.p: Fourteen tracks on RVNG Intl., with [[Juana Molina|eca5dd0e-edc7-4658-85f0-762e263b4acd]] guesting; "Cosa Rara" came out in January and "Divina" in May.
years.xp: The Skinny gave it five stars; Clash gave it 8/10 and called it "something strange and eerie, yet surprisingly close to a pop album".

years.p: Another soundtrack release for the label that put out The Seed and The Baby; she also put out the Caes EP on RVNG Intl.
